paragraphs: First check whether you accept manufacturing-site materials, equipment and repetitive quality control: potters operate potter's wheels, pug mills, glazing equipment and kilns, and finished pieces must pass drying and firing inspection.

Glazing｜mix and apply glaze to the process｜dust and chemicals follow safety rules.

paragraphs:

values: Materials｜entirely fictional｜30-minute paper exercise

P batch of 20 ceramic cups numbered P01–P20. Forming appearance record: P01–P18 have no visible defects listed in the task, P19 has a visible crack at the cup rim and P20 has a visible crack on the cup wall; only forming appearance is inspected here.

The task provides no per-piece dimensions, actual drying completion, glaze recipe, kiln temperature, equipment status or operating authorization evidence. These cannot be presumed conforming and a firing good-piece rate cannot be calculated.
All pieces, batches and data are editorial fictions; write the log only and do not touch real wheels, raw materials, glaze or kilns.
Task and deliverable｜work independently first
In the first 10 minutes write a three-row quality table: P01–P18, P19, P20, each listing the count, forming observation, current status and next step; each row can be expanded by number.

In the next 10 minutes check the inputs, forming appearance passes, count of isolated cracked pieces and forming pass rate; list separately the drying, glaze process, kiln status and authority pending card.
In the last 10 minutes write the handover summary and one review request; do not fill in real kiln temperatures, defect causes or a final release conclusion.
Reference answer｜look only after completing

P01–P18: 18 pieces in total pass forming appearance, with drying and later processes still pending verification; P19 is 1 piece with a cup rim crack and P20 is 1 piece with a cup wall crack, isolated separately pending defect review and not treated as passing pieces.
Inputs 20=18 forming appearance passes + 2 isolated cracked pieces; the forming appearance pass rate is 18/20=90%. No firing result is given, so the firing good-piece rate cannot be calculated.
Pending card: drying evidence, glaze and process version, kiln temperature and equipment status, operating authorization; all unknown, with no invented parameters and no firing decision.

Handover: P batch 20 pieces, 18 forming appearance passes only, the cracked pieces P19/P20 isolated; ask the quality role to review defect handling and the process and equipment responsible roles to check drying, process, kiln and authority, then update under site rules.

Four review items scored 0–2 each: numbered counts, crack location isolation, process and unknown boundaries, and clear handover roles. 2 points is correct and complete, 1 point is partly correct but with omissions, 0 points is wrong or missing; the maximum of 8 points is for this exercise only.
Boundaries and review
There is no evidence for the crack cause, so it can only be listed as pending verification; rework or scrap is decided by the real process and authorized roles, not on paper.
18 forming appearance passes are not firing passes and do not mean the 18 have been cleared for the kiln. 90% is a fictional inspection result, not a typical factory good-piece rate.
Ask another person to review the numbering, 20=18+2, 90%, pending items and handover; the paper work sample grants no equipment, safety or final release authority.

subject.name: Potters, Manufacturing
subject.summary: Potters, manufacturing operate pug mills, potter's wheels, forming equipment and kilns to turn clay into pottery, stoneware or other ceramic products, and must control forming, drying, glazing, firing and inspection. O*NET 51-9195.05 describes the specific potter tasks; for US wages and employment only broader BLS 51-9195 data were obtained, so the broad occupation values cannot be called potter-specific.
